title: Backup Run Manifest
description: Authoritative record of a backup run, written to the backup target at <prefix>/manifest/latest.json. Read by the freshness check. The single plaintext object in the bucket (design D11), valid only because it carries no credentials and no PII.

run_id.description: Opaque unique id for this run.

environment.description: Profile/environment that produced this manifest. The freshness reader MUST reject a manifest whose environment differs from its own. Without this, a staging run against a shared bucket overwrites the production freshness signal with its own fresh timestamp — production backups could stop entirely while /ready keeps reporting ok.

completed_at.description: UTC completion time. Input to the staleness calculation, but NOT sufficient alone — overall_outcome must also be consulted, or a fresh partial run reads as healthy.

prefix.description: Object key prefix. Never a credential-bearing URL.

retention_tier.description: Tier this run's artifacts were written under. Age-based lifecycle expiry cannot express a 7/4/12 grandfather-father-son policy over one flat prefix, so the tier is decided at write time and encoded in the key.

reason.description: Why the store was skipped or failed. Closed, log-safe text; never a raw exception or command line.

then.description: A succeeded store MUST carry size and digest. Without this a manifest omitting both validates, and an empty or truncated upload is indistinguishable from a good one.
